request.spec:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A transfer to a sheet that already has a person with the same name or alias (as names are
compared) now merges the arriving person into them instead of being refused, exactly as a merge
does (claims after theirs, aliases joined, bound figures lost); the other sheet writes
PERSON_TRANSFERRED name=<name> from=<sheet id> then PERSON_MERGED from=<name> into=<name>.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Transferring a person to a sheet that already has someone with one of their names now merges them into that person instead of refusing. `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works now**
- **Matching:** the arriving person's name and each of their aliases is compared, ignoring case, with every name and alias on the other sheet. If any match, the transfer turns into a merge into that person.
- **Merge result:** it behaves like a merge.
  - Their claims are listed after the existing person's and get the next numbers on that sheet, in the order they were opened.
  - Anything a statement had bound is cleared on those claims.
  - Their name and aliases become the existing person's aliases.
  - Their grades, terms, contact and retirement are dropped, along with everything a transfer already drops.
  - They leave the original sheet.
- **Audit:** the other sheet records `PERSON_TRANSFERRED … name=<name> from=<sheet>`, then `PERSON_MERGED … from=<name> into=<name>`, then its usual figures lines. The original sheet's records are unchanged.
- **Response:** the endpoint returns the person they merged into.

**Decisions you may want to check** (the request didn't cover these cases):
- If the arriving person's names match **more than one** person on the other sheet, the transfer is still refused.
- If the person they would merge into is **retired**, it's refused, the same as a normal merge.
- The **contact clash check** is skipped when merging, because a merge drops the contact anyway. It still applies to a plain transfer.
- When aliases are joined, one that the existing person already has **spelled exactly the same** isn't added twice. Ones that differ only in case are kept: the test expects `Ad, Addie, addie`.

**Database change:** the test's expected `Addie, addie` broke a rule that alias spellings on a sheet must differ by more than letter case. Migration `V67__alias_unique_exact.sql` relaxes it so only identical spellings are blocked. The app still refuses a new alias that differs only in case. The one gap is that two people adding such aliases at the same moment could both get through.

The work is in `PersonTransferrer.transferInto` and changes to `CheckTransfer`, `PersonTransfer`, `TransferPerson`, `RecordPersonTransferred` and `RespondWithTransfer`. I also updated the endpoint's YAML description and a comment in the transfer front-end component.
